What happens to my Microsoft / Outlook when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: Microsoft won't release a deceased person's Outlook.com or OneDrive content without a valid subpoena or court order, and even then it isn't guaranteed. You don't need to report the death. If nobody signs in, Outlook.com and OneDrive are frozen after 1 year, with content deleted soon after, and the Microsoft account expires after 2 years.

Key facts

  • Content release: subpoena or court order only
  • Outlook.com/OneDrive frozen after 1 year inactive
  • Account expires after 2 years inactive
  • Closed accounts can be reopened within 60 days

How do I prepare my Microsoft / Outlook account?

  1. Store your Microsoft password in a password manager with emergency access, so someone you trust can close the account.
  2. Export important email and OneDrive files periodically.
  3. After a death: if you have the password you can close the account yourself; Microsoft says you don't need to report the death.
  4. Without access: cancel Microsoft subscriptions through the bank, and get legal advice if you need the content (a subpoena or court order is required).

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • If you have the password: nothing; you can close the account yourself
  • Without access: a valid subpoena or court order served on Microsoft's registered agent (Microsoft won't act on faxed or emailed requests)

How long does it take?

1 year of inactivity: Outlook.com and OneDrive frozen and content deleted shortly after. 2 years: the Microsoft account expires. After a closure, 60 days to change your mind before permanent deletion.

What can't be recovered?

  • Email and OneDrive files, after the 1-year freeze and deletion
  • All account data 60 days after closure

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Microsoft / Outlook when I die?

Microsoft won't release a deceased person's Outlook.com or OneDrive content without a valid subpoena or court order, and even then it isn't guaranteed. You don't need to report the death. If nobody signs in, Outlook.com and OneDrive are frozen after 1 year, with content deleted soon after, and the Microsoft account expires after 2 years.

Can I get into my late parent's Outlook account?

Usually only with a court order, unless a legacy feature or password was planned in advance.

Does Microsoft have a legacy contact feature?

Microsoft's official page on deceased users doesn't describe one. It points family to closing the account (if they have the password) or a court order. Plan with a password manager instead.

How do I stop a dead person's Microsoft subscriptions?

Microsoft suggests cancelling via the bank: close the card or account, or revoke the payment authorisation.
